dogecoin.text:
@intangiblecoins @glxyresearch Great report. Thanks for sharing. Learned a good deal about Dogecoin from this.
Not very important but Pg 15 “Lack of Infrastructure” and “ Unsophisticated community” are identical. Curious what the essay actually says about the community.

@imperative_the @iamDJPenguin @BillyM2k Speculators in any particular token want everybody to come to their token, which will increase its relative scarcity. Presence of other tokens dilutes that. That's why there is this tribalistic behavior, e.g. Bitcoin vs Dogecoin, or ETH vs ADA.
@BillyM2k This right here gives me a lot more confidence in $Doge than in that coin named after a 19th century mathematician. 😉

@Dogecoinrich Launch a massively distributed supercomputer into orbit that mines $Doge using sunlight and then link it through Starlink to terrestrial systems.
Of course, such a computer can do other things too.

@Doge_Coin_1 @nyeapunomed Or say it with a picture
https://t.co/yqNmTHtRLO

@itsALLrisky This is the only correct take. Thanks for putting this out there. Tired of seeing the “limited supply” stupidity from maxis. Dogecoin. Has. A. Limited. Supply.
It’s disinflationary in nature.

@CEOAdam Absolutely. $Doge has a moderately disinflationary model unlike Bitcoin and is more likely to be actually used as currency. Many establishments already accept Dogecoin, most notably @mcuban and his Dallas Mavericks organization. It also has the support of Elon Musk.
